name: @macintacos/caret
description: A Claude Code plugin that replaces the terminal plan-approval prompt with a local web UI for inline review, annotation, and approval.

pinned.//: bun.lock is committed, so it is what pins every dependency exactly; a range above is the upgrade policy, not the resolved version. A bare version therefore means `bun update` must never move this one on its own, and these entries are the whole set. Everything else takes a range deliberately — zod and the TOML parser reading the config.toml trust boundary included: the lockfile already holds them, so a range costs no reproducibility and keeps them visible to an upgrade sweep. test/structure/exact-pin.test.ts fails on an exact pin with no reason, and on a reason that outlived its pin.
pinned.@pierre/diffs: Version-coupled to shiki through the resolve.alias block in ui/vite.config.ts, where an alias that stops matching grows the bundle by ~600 KB silently rather than failing anything. The pair moves as one reviewed bump, never on a sweep.
pinned.@pierre/trees: No stable release exists — the `latest` and `beta` dist-tags both point at the same prerelease. Exact rather than caret because a prerelease under a caret range is still a caret range: `^1.0.0-beta.6` expands to `>=1.0.0-beta.6 <2.0.0-0`, so a sweep would take a stable 1.0.0 the day it lands, and beta-to-stable is the jump that wants a human.

held.//: A dependency whose range deliberately stops below the current major, with the evidence for that and the condition that lifts it. Distinct from `pinned` above, which is about exact versions: an entry here names a range that is doing its job by excluding something. Unlike a pin, a held range is self-describing to `bun outdated` — it shows up as a major behind — so this block answers the question that raises rather than surfacing a decision nothing else would show.
held.typescript: Held at ^6 rather than 7.x (npm `latest` since 2026-07-08; the Go port). caret's own code is not the blocker — under 7.0.2 the root program type-checks with 0 errors and `biome lint` is clean. Two things break, both because 7.x's npm package drops the classic JS API: its `.` export is now `lib/version.cjs`, so `import ts from "typescript"` yields only `{version, versionMajorMinor}` and the compiler API moves behind `./unstable/*` subpaths. First, svelte-check 4.7.6 (its current latest) hard-throws from bin/ts-version-check.js before checking anything when `typescript` is major >= 7 — and svelte-check is the only type-checker over the Svelte half. Second, test/structure/e2e-conventions.test.ts and test/structure/tokenize-conventions.test.ts drive that API at runtime and die on `ts.ScriptTarget` being undefined. svelte-check does support 7.x, but only via `--tsgo` with `typescript` kept at 6 and 7 aliased in as @typescript/native — which is a second install rather than a move, and leaves this range at ^6 either way. Lift when a svelte-check release type-checks Svelte against a plain `typescript@7` (check with `bun pm view svelte-check peerDependencies`; today it reads `^5.0.0 || ^6.0.0`), and port the two structure tests to `typescript/unstable/ast` at the same time. Full evidence: EXC-1083.
